canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o = (W, B_W, M, X, Y, ∂, A, G, Π_X, Π_Y, r_X, r_Y, Im), where W is the rectangular entanglement matrix of a loop-symmetric state and B_W is a direct-sum/tensor-product block decomposition of the vector space containing W.
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact block-structure statement for the rectangular entanglement matrix W = Σ_{{g}_X,{g}_Y} Ψ_{{g}_X,{g}_Y}|{g}_X⟩⟨{g}_Y| of a bipartite quantum many-body state |Ψ⟩ = Σ_{{g}_X,{g}_Y} Ψ_{{g}_X,{g}_Y}|{g}_X⟩|{g}_Y⟩ on a finite lattice discretising a connected compact closed d-dimensional manifold M with d an integer satisfying d ≥ 2. The lattice has oriented edges E, vertices V, finite group G, and edge Hilbert space span{|g⟩ : g ∈ G}. The bipartition is M = X ∪ Y with X and Y complementary submanifolds, common boundary ∂ = X ∩ Y, no common edges, vertex sets V_X, V_Y, V_∂, and a base-point set A ⊂ V_∂ containing exactly one base point on each connected component of ∂. The loop-symmetry constraint is Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩ = d_α|Ψ⟩ for every irreducible representation α of G and every closed loop ℓ whose homotopy class [ℓ] is the unit element [pt] in π_1(M), with d_α the dimension of α. The desired end-state is the assertion that W belongs to ⊕_{ϕ∈Im} ⊕_{j=1}^{|G|^{|V_∂|-|A|}} C^{|r_X^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_X|} × |r_Y^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_Y|}}, equivalently (⊕_{ϕ∈Im} C^{|r_X^{-1}(ϕ)|×|r_Y^{-1}(ϕ)|}) ⊗ (⊕_{j=1}^{|G|^{|V_∂|-|A|}} C^{|G|^{|V_X|}×|G|^{|V_Y|}}), where Π_X and Π_Y are the restrictions Hom(π_1(M,A),G) → Hom(π_1(X,A),G) and Hom(π_1(M,A),G) → Hom(π_1(Y,A),G), r_X and r_Y are the restrictions Hom(π_1(X,A),G) → Hom(π_1(∂,A),G) and Hom(π_1(Y,A),G) → Hom(π_1(∂,A),G), and Im is the common image of r_X∘Π_X and r_Y∘Π_Y in Hom(π_1(∂,A),G).
feasibility_constraints: M is a connected compact closed d-dimensional manifold with d ∈ Z and d ≥ 2; a finite lattice discretisation of M has vertex set V, oriented edge set E, and plaquette set P; each edge e ∈ E carries a local Hilbert space span{|g⟩ : g ∈ G} for a finite group G.

For every closed oriented loop ℓ contained in the edge set, the Wilson-loop operator Λ^α_ℓ = Σ_{{g}_ℓ} Tr[D^α(g_1^{s_1})···D^α(g_|ℓ|^{s_|ℓ|})]|{g}_ℓ⟩⟨{g}_ℓ| is defined for each irreducible unitary representation α of G, where D^α is the representation matrix, s_i = 1 when the i-th edge orientation agrees with ℓ and s_i = -1 when it is opposite.
The state |Ψ⟩ is loop-symmetric: Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩ = d_α|Ψ⟩ for every irreducible representation α of G and every loop ℓ with [ℓ] = [pt] in π_1(M), so every contractible Wilson loop has trivial holonomy.

The bipartition satisfies M = X ∪ Y, ∂ = X ∩ Y, X and Y have no common edges, and X, Y, and ∂ are regular enough to be represented by complementary submanifolds with shared boundary; V_X and V_Y are the interior vertex sets of X and Y, and V_∂ is the boundary vertex set.

The base-point set A ⊂ V_∂ contains exactly one vertex from each connected component of ∂; π_1(Z,A) denotes the fundamental groupoid of a space Z with object set A; Hom(π_1(Z,A),G) is the set of groupoid homomorphisms from π_1(Z,A) to the one-object groupoid determined by G.

The square of inclusions ∂ → X, ∂ → Y, X → M, and Y → M is mapped by π_1(-,A) to a pushout square of groupoids and by Hom(-,G) to a pullback square of sets, so Hom(π_1(M,A),G) = {(ϕ_X,ϕ_Y) : ϕ_X ∈ Hom(π_1(X,A),G), ϕ_Y ∈ Hom(π_1(Y,A),G), r_X(ϕ_X)=r_Y(ϕ_Y)}.

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claim covers every finite group G, including Abelian and non-Abelian cases, every integer spatial dimension d ≥ 2, every connected compact closed manifold M in that dimension, every regular bipartition M = X ∪ Y with common boundary ∂, and every loop-symmetric state obeying Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩ = d_α|Ψ⟩ for all irreducible α of G and all contractible loops ℓ.

source_span.paragraph_or_line: abstract; final two paragraphs before Section II
source_span.verbatim: A general framework based on elementary algebraic topology and category theory is developed to determine the block structure of reduced density matrices for arbitrary bipartite manifolds on which the states are defined. ... Our approach applies to arbitrary space dimensions, general (sub)manifolds that can even be non-orientable, and all the finite-group-representation symmetries which are generally non-invertible.

source_span.verbatim: This includes at least two directions: one is general higher-form symmetries beyond loop symmetries, the other is general categorical symmetries beyond Rep(G) symmetries.

canonical_goal.target_object: An exact gauge-invariant refinement of the entanglement block structure for finite-group topological gauge theories on a finite lattice over M=X∪Y. The finite group is G; M is a connected compact closed d-dimensional manifold with d∈Z and d≥2; each edge carries span{|g⟩:g∈G}; the state is both loop-symmetric, Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩=d_α|Ψ⟩ for every irreducible α of G and every loop ℓ with [ℓ]=[pt] in π_1(M), and invariant under vertex gauge transformations by G. For g=(g_1,...,g_|A|)∈G^{|A|} and φ∈Hom(π_1(Z,A),G), the base-point gauge action is (g·φ)(f_{ij})=g_jφ(f_{ij})g_i^{-1} for every groupoid morphism f_{ij} from base point i to base point j. For each boundary label ϕ∈Im⊆Hom(π_1(∂,A),G), let [ϕ]={g·ϕ:g∈G^{|A|}}, let G_ϕ={g∈G^{|A|}:g·ϕ=ϕ}, and let D^X_ϕ and D^Y_ϕ be the permutation representations of G_ϕ on r_X^{-1}(ϕ) and r_Y^{-1}(ϕ). Decompose D^X_ϕ(g_ϕ)=⊕_{α_ϕ∈Rep(G_ϕ)}1_{x_{α_ϕ}}⊗D^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ) and D^Y_ϕ(g_ϕ)=⊕_{α_ϕ∈Rep(G_ϕ)}1_{y_{α_ϕ}}⊗D^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ), with x_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σ_{g_ϕ∈G_ϕ}χ^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ)TrD^X_ϕ(g_ϕ) and y_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σ_{g_ϕ∈G_ϕ}χ^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ)TrD^Y_ϕ(g_ϕ). The desired end-state is the gauge-invariant topological decomposition ⊕_{[ϕ]∈Im/G^{|A|}}1_{|[ϕ]|}⊗(⊕_{α_ϕ∈Rep(G_ϕ)}C^{x_{α_ϕ}×y_{α_ϕ}}⊗1_{d_{α_ϕ}}). For a rank-one minimally entangled block labelled by ([ϕ],α_[ϕ]), the topological entropy correction is Γ=|A|ln|G|−ln(|[ϕ]|d_{α_[ϕ]}). For a general state with small matrices Ψ_{α_[ϕ]} and singular values |ψ_{α_[ϕ],i}|^2 of Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}†, N=Σ_{[ϕ]}|[ϕ]|Σ_{α_[ϕ]}d_{α_[ϕ]}Tr(Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}†) and Γ=|A|ln|G|+Σ_{[ϕ]}|[ϕ]|Σ_{α_[ϕ]}d_{α_[ϕ]}Σ_i(|ψ_{α_[ϕ],i}|^2/N)ln(|ψ_{α_[ϕ],i}|^2/N).
feasibility_constraints: M is a connected compact closed d-dimensional manifold with d∈Z and d≥2; the finite lattice discretising M has vertex set V, oriented edge set E, boundary vertex set V_∂, and edge Hilbert spaces span{|g⟩:g∈G} for a finite group G; M=X∪Y is a regular bipartition with ∂=X∩Y, no shared edges, and base-point set A⊂V_∂ containing exactly one point on each connected component of ∂; the state |Ψ⟩ satisfies Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩=d_α|Ψ⟩ for every irreducible representation α of G and every loop ℓ with [ℓ]=[pt] in π_1(M).

Gauge invariance means the amplitude matrix W is invariant under vertex gauge transformations generated by functions from vertices to G; at base points this induces the explicit action (g·φ)(f_{ij}) = g_j φ(f_{ij}) g_i^{-1} on Hom(π_1(Z,A),G), where g=(g_1,...,g_|A|) ∈ G^{|A|} and f_{ij} is any morphism from base point i to base point j.
For each ϕ ∈ Im ⊆ Hom(π_1(∂,A),G), the stabilizer G_ϕ = {g ∈ G^{|A|} : g·ϕ=ϕ} is finite, so its irreducible representations α_ϕ, characters χ^{α_ϕ}, and dimensions d_{α_ϕ} are well-defined.

D^X_ϕ and D^Y_ϕ are the permutation representations induced by the action of G_ϕ on the finite sets r_X^{-1}(ϕ) and r_Y^{-1}(ϕ); the multiplicities x_{α_ϕ} and y_{α_ϕ} are non-negative integers determined by the finite character sums |G_ϕ|^{-1}Σ_{g_ϕ∈G_ϕ}χ^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ)TrD^{X/Y}_ϕ(g_ϕ).

The reduced density matrix on X is computed as ρ_X = W_gi W_gi† after including the geometric factor 1_{|G|^{|V_∂|-|A|}}⊗1_{|G|^{|V_X|}×|G|^{|V_Y|}}, whose nonzero spectral contribution is a degeneracy factor fixed by |G|, |V_∂|, and |A|.

source_span.verbatim: By further incorporating gauge invariance, we refine our framework to determine the entanglement structure for topological gauge theories in arbitrary dimensions. ... our setup becomes a topological gauge theory, which reduces to the Kitaev quantum double model in 2D.

hinted_superfamily.definition: Δ_hinted = {gauge-invariant generalized-symmetry entanglement problems in which the gauge constraints are higher-form or categorical constraints whose local-system data are not determined solely by Hom(π_1(-,A),G), including cases where boundary labels require higher homotopy groups or non-Rep(G) categorical data}.

source_span.verbatim: We expect that, as the Seifert–van Kampen theorem concerns the fundamental group, its extension to higher homotopy groups would allow one to compute the entanglement structure for general higher-form gauge theories through the same algorithmic procedure developed here.

The entropy component succeeds when the spectrum of ρ_X=W_giW_gi† yields Γ=|A|ln|G|−ln(|[ϕ]|d_{α_ϕ}) for a rank-one block and Γ=|A|ln|G|+Σ_{[ϕ]}|[ϕ]|Σ_{α_[ϕ]}d_{α_[ϕ]}Σ_i(|ψ_{α_[ϕ],i}|^2/N)ln(|ψ_{α_[ϕ],i}|^2/N) for a general block decomposition with N=Σ_{[ϕ]}|[ϕ]|Σ_{α_[ϕ]}d_{α_[ϕ]}Tr(Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}Ψ_{α_[ϕ]}†).

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o = (x_{α_ϕ}, y_{α_ϕ}, S, ι, D(G)-labelled entanglement-spectrum multiplicities) for two-dimensional gauge-invariant Rep(G) loop-symmetric states, including orientable and non-orientable subsystem surfaces.
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact two-dimensional specialization proving that the full entanglement-spectrum block multiplicities of the finite-group Kitaev quantum double model coincide with the Hilbert-space dimensions generated by the anyon labels of the finite-group quantum double. For a boundary with n disjoint cycles, let ϕ=(c_1,...,c_n) ∈ G^n, let [c_j] be the conjugacy class of c_j, let C_{c_j}={h∈G:h c_j=c_j h}, let α_j be an irreducible representation of C_{c_j}, and let α_ϕ=(α_1,...,α_n). For an orientable subsystem X of genus γ_X with n boundary components, the target multiplicity is x_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)} S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−2γ_X−n} Π_{j=1}^n S_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}. For a non-orientable subsystem X with k_X crosscaps and n boundary components, the target multiplicity is x_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)} ι_β^{k_X} S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−k_X−n} Π_{j=1}^n S_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}. Here [g] ranges over conjugacy classes in G, C_g={h∈G:hg=gh}, β ranges over irreducible representations of C_g, d_β is the dimension of β, χ^β is its character, ι_β=|C_g|^{-1}Σ_{t∈C_g}χ^β(t^2), and S_{(g,β),(c,α)}=(|C_g||C_c|)^{-1}Σ_{h∈G, h^{-1}gh∈C_c} χ^β(hch^{-1})χ^α(h^{-1}gh). The end-state is exact equality between these multiplicities and the remaining internal degrees of freedom in the entanglement spectrum; this realizes the Li-Haldane proposition that the full entanglement spectrum carries the same sector-counting structure as the corresponding two-dimensional rational conformal field-theory boundary Hilbert space for the finite-group quantum double.
feasibility_constraints: G is a finite group; M is a compact two-dimensional surface with a finite oriented-edge lattice whose edge Hilbert spaces are span{|g⟩:g∈G}; M=X∪Y with compact subsystem surfaces X and Y and common one-dimensional boundary ∂=X∩Y consisting of n disjoint cycles with n∈Z and n≥1; the state is invariant under contractible Rep(G) Wilson-loop operators Λ^α_ℓ and under vertex gauge transformations by G, so it is a finite-group flat lattice gauge state of the type that in two spatial dimensions realizes the Kitaev quantum double construction.

Boundary labels are ϕ=(c_1,...,c_n) ∈ G^n; for each c_j, the centralizer is C_{c_j}={h∈G:h c_j=c_j h}; the stabilizer of ϕ under simultaneous boundary conjugation is G_ϕ=C_{c_1}×···×C_{c_n}; irreducible representations of G_ϕ are tensor products α_ϕ=(α_1,...,α_n) with α_j∈Rep(C_{c_j}).

The matrix S is fixed internally by S_{(g,β),(c,α)}=(|C_g||C_c|)^{-1}Σ_{h∈G, h^{-1}gh∈C_c}χ^β(hch^{-1})χ^α(h^{-1}gh), where g,c∈G, β∈Rep(C_g), α∈Rep(C_c), χ^β and χ^α are the corresponding characters, and C_g and C_c are centralizers in G.

For an orientable X, γ_X is the non-negative integer such that X is a connected orientable surface with γ_X handles and n boundary circles; for a non-orientable X, k_X is the positive integer such that X is a connected non-orientable surface with k_X crosscaps and n boundary circles.

The Frobenius-Schur indicator used in the non-orientable formula is defined by ι_β=|C_g|^{-1}Σ_{t∈C_g}χ^β(t^2), with ι_β ∈ {-1,0,1}; no external classification theorem is required to evaluate the formula once G, g, β, c_j, and α_j are specified.

success_set.definition: Σ_P = {o : G is finite; M is a compact two-dimensional surface partitioned as M=X∪Y with ∂=X∩Y containing n≥1 disjoint boundary cycles; the state is invariant under contractible Rep(G) Wilson loops and vertex gauge transformations; for every boundary label ϕ=(c_1,...,c_n)∈G^n and every α_ϕ=(α_1,...,α_n) with α_j∈Rep(C_{c_j}), the entanglement-spectrum multiplicity for an orientable X of genus γ_X is x_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)}S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−2γ_X−n}Π_{j=1}^nS_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}; the entanglement-spectrum multiplicity for a non-orientable X with k_X crosscaps is x_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)}ι_β^{k_X}S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−k_X−n}Π_{j=1}^nS_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}; the multiplicity for an orientable Y of genus γ_Y is y_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)}S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−2γ_Y−n}Π_{j=1}^nS_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}; the multiplicity for a non-orientable Y with k_Y crosscaps is y_{α_ϕ}=Σ_{[g]}Σ_{β∈Rep(C_g)}ι_β^{k_Y}S_{(g,β),(1,1)}^{2−k_Y−n}Π_{j=1}^nS_{(g,β),(c_j,α_j)}; S_{(g,β),(c,α)}=(|C_g||C_c|)^{-1}Σ_{h∈G,h^{-1}gh∈C_c}χ^β(hch^{-1})χ^α(h^{-1}gh); ι_β=|C_g|^{-1}Σ_{t∈C_g}χ^β(t^2); a block labelled by ([ϕ],α_ϕ) appears in the full entanglement spectrum exactly when x_{α_ϕ}>0 and y_{α_ϕ}>0; these same finite sums count the finite-group quantum-double boundary-label Hilbert-space sectors for the labels ([c_j],α_j) }.

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claim covers the two-dimensional Kitaev quantum double model for arbitrary finite group G, arbitrary orientable subsystem surfaces with any non-negative genus γ and any positive number n of boundary cycles, and arbitrary non-orientable subsystem surfaces with any positive crosscap number k and any positive number n of boundary cycles, provided the bipartition is compatible with a finite lattice and the boundary labels ϕ=(c_1,...,c_n) are evaluated by the stated centralizer and S-matrix formulas.

methodological_claim.target_object: The derivation method converts the topological gluing data of a bipartition M=X∪Y with ∂=X∩Y into algebraic boundary-sector data by applying π_1(-,A) to obtain a pushout square of fundamental groupoids and then applying Hom(-,G) to obtain a pullback square of finite sets; after gauge invariance is imposed, the same pullback is promoted to a pullback of G^{|A|}-sets and the residual invariant blocks are computed by finite stabilizer-orbit decompositions and irreducible character sums. This is a derivational pipeline rather than an additional physical end-state: it specifies how the loop-symmetric block structure, the gauge-invariant orbit/stabilizer refinement, and the two-dimensional sector-counting formulas are obtained.

evidence_channels.formalisation: Given inclusions ∂→X, ∂→Y, X→M, and Y→M with base points A⊂∂, compute π_1(M,A), π_1(X,A), π_1(Y,A), and π_1(∂,A). The groupoid square π_1(∂,A)→π_1(X,A), π_1(∂,A)→π_1(Y,A), π_1(X,A)→π_1(M,A), π_1(Y,A)→π_1(M,A) is used as a pushout. Applying Hom(-,G) gives Hom(π_1(M,A),G) = Hom(π_1(X,A),G) ×_{Hom(π_1(∂,A),G)} Hom(π_1(Y,A),G). With gauge invariance, equip each Hom set with the action (g·φ)(f_{ij})=g_jφ(f_{ij})g_i^{-1}; quotient by orbits, compute stabilizers G_ϕ, decompose the induced permutation representations by finite character sums, and read off the invariant entanglement blocks.

source_span.paragraph_or_line: abstract; final paragraph before Section II
source_span.verbatim: A rigorous analysis is presented for the entanglement spectrum of quantum many-body states possessing a higher-form group-representation symmetry generated by topological Wilson loops, which is generally non-invertible. A general framework based on elementary algebraic topology and category theory is developed to determine the block structure of reduced density matrices for arbitrary bipartite manifolds on which the states are defined. ... In this work, we develop a general and rigorous framework for analyzing entanglement structures of quantum many-body states that respect such generalized symmetries.

stated_goal.formalisation: Stated-goal formalisation: (i) for every finite group G, every d∈Z with d≥2, every connected compact closed M, every regular bipartition M=X∪Y with ∂=X∩Y, every base-point set A⊂∂ containing one base point per boundary component, and every state satisfying Λ^α_ℓ|Ψ⟩=d_α|Ψ⟩ for all irreducible α and all loops ℓ with [ℓ]=[pt] in π_1(M), W lies in ⊕_{ϕ∈Im}⊕_{j=1}^{|G|^{|V_∂|-|A|}}C^{|r_X^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_X|}×|r_Y^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_Y|}}; (ii) for the same finite-group lattice data with additional vertex-gauge invariance, the topological part is ⊕_{[ϕ]}1_{|[ϕ]|}⊗(⊕_{α_ϕ}C^{x_{α_ϕ}×y_{α_ϕ}}⊗1_{d_{α_ϕ}}) with x_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σ_{g_ϕ∈G_ϕ}χ^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ)TrD^X_ϕ(g_ϕ) and y_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σ_{g_ϕ∈G_ϕ}χ^{α_ϕ}(g_ϕ)TrD^Y_ϕ(g_ϕ); and (iii) in two dimensions for a finite-group flat lattice gauge state on a surface with n boundary cycles, these x and y multiplicities equal the orientable and non-orientable finite sums built from S_{(g,β),(c,α)}=(|C_g||C_c|)^{-1}Σ_{h∈G,h^{-1}gh∈C_c}χ^β(hch^{-1})χ^α(h^{-1}gh) and ι_β=|C_g|^{-1}Σ_{t∈C_g}χ^β(t^2).

operational_goal.formalisation: Operational-goal formalisation: compute W and ρ_X blocks exactly. For loop symmetry alone, W∈⊕_{ϕ∈Im}⊕_{j=1}^{|G|^{|V_∂|-|A|}}C^{|r_X^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_X|}×|r_Y^{-1}(ϕ)||G|^{|V_Y|}} with Im=image(r_X∘Π_X)=image(r_Y∘Π_Y). With vertex-gauge invariance, quotient boundary labels by (g·ϕ)(f_{ij})=g_jϕ(f_{ij})g_i^{-1}, compute G_ϕ={g∈G^{|A|}:g·ϕ=ϕ}, compute x_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σχ^{α_ϕ}TrD^X_ϕ and y_{α_ϕ}=|G_ϕ|^{-1}Σχ^{α_ϕ}TrD^Y_ϕ, and obtain ⊕_{[ϕ]}1_{|[ϕ]|}⊗(⊕_{α_ϕ}C^{x_{α_ϕ}×y_{α_ϕ}}⊗1_{d_{α_ϕ}}). In d=2, evaluate x and y by the explicit S-matrix and Frobenius-Schur formulas for orientable and non-orientable subsystem surfaces.

inference_basis: The abstract, introduction, and summary repeatedly identify the end-state as entanglement block structure or full entanglement-spectrum structure, not as optimization, simulation, or numerical performance.
The central equations (11), (12), (44), (46), (49), (51), and (53) are closed-form structural propositions about W, ρ_X, topological entropy, and sector multiplicities.
Worked examples for torus, genus surfaces, Klein bottle, lens spaces, and higher-dimensional tori serve as instantiations of the same block-structure target rather than independent objectives.
The gauge-invariant and Li-Haldane results are downstream specializations of the general pullback/block framework, so the best multi-goal relation is instrumental rather than independent.
implicit_goal.formalisation: Implicit-goal formalisation: the best-fitting end-state is an instrumental three-stage target proposition: first, determine the direct-sum/tensor-product block structure of W for states satisfying finite-group Rep(G) Wilson-loop symmetry on contractible loops; second, impose vertex-gauge invariance to obtain the orbit/stabilizer/irrep block structure of W_gi and ρ_X together with Γ=|A|ln|G|−ln(|[ϕ]|d_{α_[ϕ]}) for rank-one blocks and the singular-value correction formula for general blocks; third, in two spatial dimensions, show that the gauge-invariant multiplicities x_{α_ϕ},y_{α_ϕ} equal the finite-group quantum-double sector-counting sums built from S_{(g,β),(c,α)} and ι_β.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated channel asks for rigorous entanglement-spectrum and reduced-density-matrix block-structure analysis under finite-group representation loop symmetries, then under additional vertex-gauge invariance, and then for the two-dimensional finite-group quantum-double full-spectrum correspondence. The operational equations compute exactly those objects: the loop-symmetric W decomposition, the gauge-invariant orbit/stabilizer/irrep decomposition, the topological-entanglement-entropy formulas, and the two-dimensional S-matrix/Frobenius-Schur multiplicity formulas. Motivational statements about generalized symmetry, topological order, and future higher-categorical extensions are recorded as excluded aims or hinted superfamilies rather than as extra canonical goals.
